newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais issue arrest warrant for Saudi tycoon.
newsitem.headline: Thais issue arrest warrant for Saudi tycoon.

text.p: Thai police said on Friday they had issued arrest warrants for Saudi Arabian tycoon Adnan Khashoggi and four other officials of the Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc on charges of conspiring to defraud the bank.

A police officer told Reuters the Bank of Thailand requested the warrants for the five on suspicion that they jointly conspired for Khashoggi to draw 2.0 billion baht ($77.5 million) in loans from the BBC without credible collateral in 1995.

Police Colonel Prachaksin Supanpaesak said warrants were issued for former Bangkok Bank of Commerce president Krirkkiat Jalichandra and former adviser Rakesh Saxena. Krirkkiat also faces other criminal charges relating to his former role in the bank, which was taken over by the government last May.

Saxena has been resident in Canada since mid-1996 when opposition politicians said in the Thai parliament that Bangkok Bank of Commerce was saddled with an unsustainable amount of non-performing loans totalling over 70 billion baht (US$2.7 billion).
The charges triggered a heavy public run on the bank's deposits and the government later took over the bank.

Khashoggi's whereabouts were unknown. Police said that a Briton, Terry Easter, had been arrested on a warrant issued in July last year charging him with conspiring to embezzle assets of Bangkok Bank of Commerce.
